Dear Senator Beebe-Center and Representative Hasenfus,
I am writing to respectfully request that the Committee issue an Ought Not to Pass recommendation for
LD 1909, "Resolve, to Provide a Comprehensive Analysis of Criminal Legal System Data."
This resolution was introduced to initiate a critical, independent analysis of how public entities in
Maine currently collect, store, and utilize data related to the criminal legal system. It aimed to identify barriers to comprehensive data collection and develop a multiphase plan to address those barriers, ultimately improving transparency and accountability within our criminal justice system.
However, after further consideration and discussions with stakeholders, it has become clear that the
proposed approach may require a more comprehensive framework to effectively address the complex
challenges associated with criminal legal system data. I believe this approach would benefit from additional collaboration with data experts, criminal justice advocates, and impacted communities before moving forward.
I remain committed to improving transparency and accountability within Maine's criminal justice system and appreciate the Committee's thoughtful consideration of this request.
Thank you for your attention to this matter.

Rachel Talbot Ross State Senator, District 28 Representing part ofPortland and Peaks Island

Senator Anne Beebe-Center, Chair Representative Tavis Hasenfus, Chair Committee on Criminal Justice and Public Safety 5 State House Station, Room 436 Augusta, ME 04333
RE: LD 1909: Resolve, to Provide a Comprehensive Analysis of Criminal Legal System Data
Dear Senator Beebe-Center, Representative Hasenfus, and Members of the Committee on Criminal Justice and Public Safety:
The Maine Association of Criminal Defense Lawyers is a non-profit organization that has nearly 300 member attorneys who practice criminal defense across the state. Since 1992, MACDL has advocated for its members and the people we are fortunate to represent in courtrooms throughout Maine and at the State House.
MACDL presents this testimony in support of LD 1909.
If passed and effectively implemented, this bill would assist the Legislature--and in turn, the people of Maine--immeasurably by requiring the collection of much necessary data from the criminal legal system and the analysis of said data. No more would it be acceptable to rely on personal anecdotes or "I wish we had that data" when considering proposals for change.
Directing law enforcement agencies, the Judicial Branch, and the Department of Corrections and local jail facilities to provide access to their data collection systems to carry out this independent study is necessary. The veils of secrecy--whether intentional or not--have led to a dearth of information on how these systems interact with and impact people across the State of Maine.
The timeline proposed in the bill appears to be sufficient for this independent study entity to collect the necessary data and to analyze it and present it in such a way that it is useful to the future iteration of this Committee. Well-informed committees do the best work--the results of this study should assist greatly in ensuring that this Committee can do its best work moving forward. Our clients depend on the Legislature to do right by them in considering bills and other proposals: operating from a point of objective data is necessary to ensure reasoned decision-making.
We urge this Committee to vote ought to pass on LD 1909.
Thank you for your consideration, for your attention to this important matter, and for allowing me to present this testimony to you all today.
